title: Installing and Evaluating Packages
learning_outcomes: Explain what installing and evaluating packages contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: packagist.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Composer describes dependencies and maps namespaces to source files. Lockfiles make application installs reproducible; declared constraints and maintenance/security review keep dependency choices intentional. In this lesson, focus on packagist; then compare it with package documentation. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use installing and evaluating packages when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Composer describes dependencies and maps namespaces to source files. Lockfiles make application installs reproducible; declared constraints and maintenance/security review keep dependency choices intentional. For installing and evaluating packages, begin with packagist. Also distinguish package documentation; dependency health; maintenance and compatibility. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.

hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.

common_mistakes.why: Updates can overwrite manual changes and make builds irreproducible.
common_mistakes.fix: Declare dependencies in composer.json and regenerate the lock/autoload state using Composer.

common_mistakes.why: Different environments may resolve different dependency versions.
common_mistakes.fix: Commit the lockfile for applications and use the project’s intended install workflow.

common_mistakes.problem: Choosing a package by download count alone.
common_mistakes.why: Popularity does not prove security, maintenance, or version compatibility.
common_mistakes.fix: Review maintenance activity, releases, dependencies, license, and docs.
